eyebrow: Saving a query as a view
code:
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW vw_unpaid_invoices_over_threshold AS
SELECT s.vendor_name, i.invoice_num, i.invoice_date, ps.due_date,
       ps.amount_remaining,
       TRUNC(SYSDATE) - ps.due_date AS days_overdue
FROM ap_invoices_all i
INNER JOIN poz_suppliers s ON s.vendor_id = i.vendor_id
INNER JOIN ap_payment_schedules_all ps ON ps.invoice_id = i.invoice_id
WHERE i.payment_status_flag <> 'Y'
  AND ps.amount_remaining > 10000
  AND TRUNC(SYSDATE) - ps.due_date > 30;
caption: Lesson 23's full challenge query, saved under a name — OR REPLACE updates it safely.

eyebrow: Reusing it, with zero knowledge of the joins
code:
SELECT * FROM vw_unpaid_invoices_over_threshold
ORDER BY days_overdue DESC;
caption: The complexity is captured once, in the view, and reused forever after.
